newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korea Dec diesel exports soar, but price holding.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Dec diesel exports soar, but price holding.

text.p: South Korean spot diesel exports in December reached a new winter record of up to 2.5 million barrels, boosted by greater refinery processing and weak domestic demand, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Sources said they expected a similar amount of spot exports in January after 2-2.5 million barrels were sold in December on top of the estimated 2.0 million barrels in term sales.
"Korean refiners have already committed at least 1.5 million barrels of diesel for export in January," one refiner said.
But so far there has been limited pressure on prices because of surging Chinese demand, traders said.
South Korea usually exports between 1-1.5 million barrels of spot diesel per month during winter, while summer exports are usualy double that due to low domestic demand.
The rise in exports was partly the result of South Korea's expanding refinery sector.

Processing capacity grew to 2.2 million barrels-per-day (bpd) in 1996 with the start up of three new crude units each with a refining capacity of at least 200,000-bpd each and their greatest impact was felt towards the end of the year.
But traders said refiners had also over estimated December middle distillate consumption as demand proved to be weak.

Unexpectedly large December kerosene imports of six milliion barrels were not matched by domestic demand. As a result, middle distillate consumption moved in favour of the better quality kerosene, instead of diesel, for heating.
Import orders for kerosene in January have been drastically cut to around two million barrels, sources said.
The bulk of the Korean diesel exports was sucked in by China, where demand has surged because of stock shortages and reduced refinery runs, a market source said.
The China demand prevented a price slide for Asian diesel.
Traders estimated 2 million barrels of Korean exports were sold into China at $250-$260 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis, the source said.
China raised December diesel imports to an estimated one million tonnes (7.5 million barrels), from a more-normal 4.5 million barrels.

The Korean exports to China were aided by the shutdown of a 40,000-bpd desulphurization unit at Hanwha Energy Ltd for 10 days in mid-December, diverting more 0.5 percent sulphur diesel onto the market.
The desulphurizer lowers the sulphur content in diesel to meet tougher Korean specifications at 0.1.
South Korea's total oil products exports grew 29 percent to 145.1 million barrels in the first 11 months of 1996, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said earlier.
The ministry said in a statement the rise reflected growth in oil products production and a slowdown in domestic demand.
Exports for loading in the second half of January were offered at about 50 cents over spot Singapore quotes on a free-on-board basis, versus 45-65 cents in December.
Traders said they expected continued China demand to underpin the price for at least the rest of January trading.
Offers were seen from all three main exporters, Yukong Ltd 45510.KS, Hanwha Energy and Hyundai Oil Refinery Co as well as onstream a new 220,000-bpd crude unit.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
